summary: Wilhelm Printz was an Indologist who studied under Wilhelm Schulze (~1906–1911) and Heinrich Lüders (~1909–1911).

Wilhelm Rau worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig under Friedrich Weller (~1940–1944) and earned his doctorate at Marburg under Johannes Nobel (1946–1949). He held professorships at Frankfurt (1955) and Marburg (1958–1987).

Wilhelm Scherer worked in linguistics. He studied at Vienna and Berlin under Moriz Haupt, Franz Bopp, and Karl Müllenhoff. He held posts at Vienna (1864, 1868–1872), Strasbourg (1872), and Berlin (1877), and joined the Prussian Academy of Sciences (1884).

Wilhelm Schmidt worked in linguistics and religious studies. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1893–1895) and later held positions at the University of Vienna (~1906–1938) and the University of Fribourg (~1939–1951).

Wilhelm Schott was a scholar of Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1823–1826) and served on the faculty there from ~1833 to 1889.

Wilhelm Schulze, a scholar of linguistics and Indology, studied at Berlin and Greifswald under Johannes Schmidt, Heinrich Zimmer, Adolf Kiessling, and Georg Kaibel. He held chairs at Marburg (1892), Göttingen (1895), and Berlin (1902–1932).

Wilhelm Solf was an Indologist who studied at Berlin, Göttingen, Jena, Halle-Wittenberg (doctoral supervisor Richard Pischel, ~1883–1885), and Kiel. He later held a post at Kiel University (~1888–1890).
Wilhelm Storck studied under Franz Bopp (~1850–1854) and Moriz Haupt (~1853–1856).

Wilhelm Streitberg worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Münster, Leipzig (under Karl Brugmann and Ernst Windisch), and Berlin. He held posts at Fribourg (~1889–1898), Münster (1899), Munich (~1909–1920), and Leipzig (1898, 1920–1925).

Wilhelm Vatke was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Halle-Wittenberg (~1825–1827), Göttingen (~1827–1828), and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1828–1830), where he later held a post from ~1834 to 1882.

Wilhelm Wackernagel was a scholar of linguistics who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (1824–1827) under Karl Lachmann and August Boeckh. He taught at Pädagogium Basel (~1833–1835) and held a professorship at the University of Basel (1833–1869).

Wilhelm Wundt worked in philosophy. He studied at Tübingen, Heidelberg (~1852–1856), and Berlin. He held positions at the University of Zurich (1857), the University of Leipzig (1858), and Heidelberg University (1864).

Wilhelm von Humboldt worked in linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Viadrina, Göttingen, and Jena under scholars including Lichtenberg and Heyne. He served at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1809–1810) and as a Prussian minister (~1819).
Will Sweetman is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at Lancaster University and the University of Cambridge (~1996–1999) and held a post at the University of Otago (~2005).

Will Tuladhar-Douglas works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Oxford. His posts include lecturing at the University of Aberdeen, directing the Scottish Centre for Himalayan Research, and serving as a research fellow at Hamburg.

Willard Gurdon Oxtoby worked in religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Stanford, Princeton, and Harvard. He held posts at McGill (1960–1964), Yale (1966–1971), and Trinity College and the University of Toronto (~1971–1999).

Willard Van Orman Quine was a philosopher and linguist. He studied at Oberlin College and Harvard University, where he spent most of his career as Junior Fellow (1933–1936), Assistant Professor (1940), and Pierce Chair of Philosophy (1948–1978).

Willem Bollée was an Indologist. He studied at Utrecht University (~1946–1956) and the University of Hamburg (~1965–1975). He served as an assistant professor at Münster (1971–1978) and as a lecturer and professor at Heidelberg University (~1977–1993).

Willem Caland worked in Indology and linguistics. He earned his doctorate at Leiden University (1877) under Carel Gabriel Cobet and Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern. He held posts at Utrecht University (1903–1929) and Leiden University (1913–1914).
Willem van der Molen works in linguistics, history/archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Leiden University (~1970–1983) and held posts at Leiden University (~1984) and the University of Indonesia.
